LESSON: IMITATION

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING AND
Topic 1.1: Imitation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Imitation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond appropriately to  Learners take turns as they participate in panel conversations with varied discussions on issues related to self, home, and audiences family

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: IMITATION
This lesson teaches Imitation for Grade 3 LITERACY ACTIVITIES.

STUDY STEPS
1. respond appropriately to  Learners take turns as they participate in panel conversations with varied discussions on issues related to self, home, and audiences family
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Imitation using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Imitation above.
2. Explain Imitation to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Imitation.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Imitation with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Imitation important for a Grade 3 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. respond appropriately to  Learners take turns as they participate in panel conversations with varied discussions on issues related to self, home, and audiences family

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
